question: What have MPs said about trial by jury?

blocks.text:
**In brief**

- The Conservative front bench pressed the Government on whether the Courts and Tribunals Bill would reduce jury access, as when Nick Timothy asked whether the Justice Secretary could
"guarantee that the Bill will not reduce access to jury trials at all?"

citations.quoted: Now that we know the Courts and Tribunals Bill will return to the House on 13 October, immediately after the recess, can the Justice Secretary guarantee that the Bill will not reduce access to jury trials at all?

blocks.text: - The Justice Secretary tied his approach to court backlogs, as when Alex Norris said
"my priority is to reduce the Crown court waiting list and enable victims to have their day in court more quickly."

citations.quoted: Last week, the Leader of the House announced that the Courts and Tribunals Bill will return to this House on 13 October. I have been clear that my priority is to reduce the Crown court waiting list and enable victims to have their day in court more quickly. I look forward to working with experts in this House and beyond to deliver that.

blocks.text: - The Liberal Democrat spokesperson raised human rights and scrutiny time, as when Jessica Brown-Fuller said
"The time is right to change course, prior to the return of the Bill in October."

citations.quoted: These issues were raised at earlier stages of the Bill, but the Government batted away our concerns. The time is right to change course, prior to the return of the Bill in October. Can the Secretary of State confirm that those concerns are being heard by the Prime Minister while he considers the future of the Bill, and can he guarantee that hon. Members from across the House and experts in the sector will have adequate time to scrutinise the Government’s amendments before we are asked to debate it on the second day back after recess?

blocks.text:
**Conservative frontbench - critical**

Conservative spokespeople challenged the Government over its jury proposals, as when Nick Timothy, Shadow Justice Secretary, quoted the Prime Minister's promise to
"find ways of not reducing access to jury trial."

citations.quoted: “find ways of not reducing access to jury trial.”

blocks.text: - Timothy also cited the Prime Minister's description of jury trials as a
"linchpin of a fair society."

- Neil Shastri-Hurst, a shadow health minister, who spoke on a justice question, referred to reports of a possible amendment under which a judge would decide on jury or single-judge trial in either-way offences. He said the legal profession had warned this
"will lead to satellite litigation, with repeated appeals, and slow down the legal process."

citations.quoted: There are reports that the Government are considering tabling an amendment to the Courts and Tribunals Bill so that, in either-way offences, a judge will decide whether a defendant faces a jury or is heard by a single judge sitting alone. The legal profession has quite properly highlighted that this will lead to satellite litigation, with repeated appeals, and slow down the legal process. Will the Government finally listen to the legal profession, or will they plough on regardless?
